summary: The v1 contract and control_api.py are sound: fail-closed remote calls with no redirects and size caps, constant-time operator auth that is off when unset, a strict input schema, sanitized summaries, and CPU_SYNTHETIC labeling with model_executed=false. Approved, subject to the follow-ups below, so that the dependent security, RAG and backend tasks can start. None of the follow-ups weakens a security boundary.
required_followups: F1 Evidence enum: the API accepts REAL_MODEL, REAL_IBM_MIA and LIVE_REAL_MODEL. Freeze a single enum in the contract: CPU_SYNTHETIC | STATIC_ESTIMATE | REAL_MODEL | REAL_IBM_MIA | NOT_CAPTURED. The claude worker now emits REAL_IBM_MIA (mia_runtime.EVIDENCE_LIVE changed to match).

F2 Kaggle is batch-only: kernels accept no inbound HTTPS, so MODEL_MOUNTAIN_REMOTE_URL cannot point at Kaggle. Live remote inference needs a separately hosted vLLM-Hook server; otherwise /jobs should be an operator-side batch adapter (kaggle push, status and output) and /reports should publish the downloaded REAL_IBM_MIA JSON. Proposal: until a hosted worker exists, the UI shows the Kaggle reports with their timestamps and 'remote: not configured'.

F3 /orchestration on Vercel reads a deploy-time .ai/TASKS.json and labels it live=true. Exclude .ai/ from the Vercel bundle (.vercelignore), or label the result as a snapshot with its revision and timestamp, never as live.

F4 /models public fallback: source the list from kaggle/model_allowlist.json plus remote_models.ModelRegistry.matrix(), which gives a STATIC_ESTIMATE with capabilities and blockers, instead of a single hardcoded Qwen2 entry.
evidence: source inspection of every route in ControlAPI.handle
